q: Is the preferred window 4 days (15–18 Feb) or a 7-night stay starting 15 Feb?
why: The brief says '1–2 weeks' but also lists 15–18 Feb 2027, which is 3 nights. Every price here is for a 7-night stay (15–22 Feb).
how: Decide the number of nights; the price table can be re-cut for 3, 4 or 7 nights in minutes.

q: Do you want the 7 nights in one hotel, or 4 nights Shanghai + 3 nights elsewhere?
why: A second city adds a train/flight and breaks the ≤60 min rule; the MICHELIN density argument only holds for one base.
how: Compare the Shanghai-only plan with a Shanghai + Suzhou/Hangzhou split (needs rail times, not yet verified).

q: What is the total budget for the two of you, excluding flights?
why: Without a ceiling, the ranking cannot trade price against Michelin density — the Waldorf/Peninsula options are 2–3.4× the Radisson.
how: Give a number; we can then recommend exactly one hotel instead of a ranking.

q: Should we keep 15 Feb even though it is two days after the 5–13 Feb Spring Festival break?
why: Residual holiday travel and possible restaurant closures; the price data nevertheless favours this week.
how: Confirm a handful of restaurant reopen dates for mid-February before committing.

q: How many MICHELIN dinners do you actually want in 7 nights?
why: Three to five starred dinners in a week is a lot of tasting menus; it also drives the budget that is currently unquantified.
how: Pick a number 1–5; the itinerary then assigns specific restaurants by their published opening days.

q: Are there dietary restrictions (vegetarian, shellfish, alcohol)?
why: Fu He Hui is vegetarian; Cantonese/Chaozhou menus are seafood-heavy; several houses are tasting-menu only.
how: List restrictions; then re-check each restaurant's menu before booking.

q: Do you hold a bank card that works in mainland China, and is Alipay/WeChat Pay set up?
why: Many restaurants and ticket desks prefer mobile payment; MICHELIN lists card acceptance per restaurant but the payment rails still matter.
how: Set up Alipay/WeChat Pay with a foreign card before departure and carry a physical card.

q: Is the visa situation confirmed for both passports?
why: Visa/entry rules change and were not verified in this build; they are a hard gate on any booking.
how: Check the Chinese embassy/consulate site for your nationality and the current visa-free rules.

q: Do you need step-free access / lift access at restaurants and stations?
why: Some MICHELIN rooms are in heritage buildings and mezzanines; the metro is not uniformly step-free.
how: State the requirement; filter restaurants by wheelchair-access tags that MICHELIN publishes.

q: Is a queen bed acceptable, or must it be a king?
why: The cheapest qualifying Radisson room has 1 queen; the Waldorf has 2 queens; the Peninsula has 1 king.
how: Confirm bed preference; it changes which room line is the 'cheapest qualifying' one.

q: Will you book refundable or non-refundable rates?
why: Non-refundable saves 20% at the Waldorf ($2,414 vs $3,018) but locks the dates.
how: Decide risk appetite; then pick the matching rate line.

q: When should we actually pull the trigger on the booking?
why: The site shows what the room costs today for five windows, not a forecast. Booking early is only 'best' if the price trend is downward — which this dataset cannot prove.
how: Set a target price (e.g. W1 Junior Suite below $1,116) and a deadline; or book a free-cancellation rate now and re-check monthly.
